## Documented role

On [24 February 1984](../sources/1984-hansard-mowat-creekview.qmd), Hansard records Mr. Mowat, speaking as a Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) in budget debate, describing six high-lesion respiratory quadriplegics about to leave Pearson Hospital for the Creekview Co-op on False Creek, with support services “plugged in,” and giving per-diem estimates before opening. That sitting does not say he designed Creekview, and it does not name CSIL or ECPM.

CSIL or ECPM design-group membership is **not** inferred from that speech or from later organizational histories.

## Later accounts

The [SCI BC history page](../sources/sci-bc-history.qmd) states that in 1960 “Doug Mowat accepts the role of Executive Director” of the British Columbia Paraplegic Association (BCPA), that the organization “flourished under his innovative, strong leadership extending over three decades,” and that he chaired the provincial International Year of the Disabled effort in 1981. [SCI Canada’s timeline](../sources/sci-can-timeline-mowat.qmd) attributes an Order of Canada (1982 entry), thirty years as CPA BC executive director, and service as MLA from 1983 to 1991. Those are later organizational attributions, not appointment records from the time.

[Fayerman 2018](../sources/2018-vancouversun-walt-lawrence.qmd) reports Walt Lawrence giving Mowat, “then MLA,” credit in connection with a CPA cost analysis and the Creekview move. [SCI BC, “Walt’s Time” (2019)](../sources/2019-sci-bc-walts-time.qmd) calls the housing cooperative “championed by SCI BC’s Doug Mowat.” Those are later wordings. See the [Creekview chapter](../history/creekview.qmd).

## Unresolved

These questions remain open. They are for documentary checks. Please do not contact surviving colleagues or other living participants unsolicited.

1. In 1984–85, was Mowat acting as MLA, as BCPA executive director, or both, in Creekview work?
2. Does he appear by name in the unread 1987 evaluation or in the April 1986 Paraplegic Association correspondence Nielsen mentioned?
3. What written CPA cost analysis, if any, did he commission or receive before opening?
4. Is there a document from the time that puts him on a later ECPM or CSIL design group? (None is inferred here.)
